stem: What does mean corpuscular volume (MCV) measure?

options.A: The total number of circulating red blood cells in a measured blood volume.
options.B: The average size or volume of circulating red blood cells.
options.C: The average amount of hemoglobin contained in each red blood cell.
options.D: The percentage of blood volume occupied by red blood cells.

rationale: MedlinePlus defines mean corpuscular volume (MCV) as a red-cell index that measures the average size of red blood cells. By contrast, the red blood cell count measures the number of circulating red cells, mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) measures the average amount of hemoglobin in a red cell, and hematocrit measures the proportion of blood volume occupied by red blood cells. Therefore B is correct.
educational_objective: Identify MCV as the red-cell index that measures average red blood cell size/volume and distinguish it from RBC count, MCH, and hematocrit.
source_organization: MedlinePlus, U.S. National Library of Medicine (NIH)
source_document_title: MCV (Mean Corpuscular Volume); Red Blood Cell (RBC) Indices
source_version_date: Current MedlinePlus resources live-rechecked August 16, 2026; RBC Indices encyclopedia review February 27, 2026
source_locator: MCV Medical Test > What is an MCV blood test?: MCV measures average size of RBCs. RBC Indices: MCV average size; MCH average hemoglobin amount per RBC. CBC/hematocrit resources distinguish RBC count and hematocrit from MCV.
source_claim_supported: MCV measures average red blood cell size/volume, not red-cell number, per-cell hemoglobin amount, or percentage of blood volume occupied by RBCs.

source_original.rationale: MCV stands for mean corpuscular volume and measures the average size of red blood cells. It is one of the red-cell indices used to help classify anemia.
